ranked.headline: Learned molecular and protein embeddings fused with graphs and language models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and JCIM papers pair pretrained protein and chemical language models with graph encoders and knowledge graphs for prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Deep learning links transcriptomic, histologic and single-cell data to biomedical outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply deep models to pathway analysis, survival prediction, histology-to-expression mapping and single-cell integration.

ranked.headline: Computational profiling of SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viral variation and host adaptation
ranked.summary: Sequence-based and host-factor analyses now link SARS-CoV-2 and influenza variation to variant classification, antigenic prediction, and adaptation.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks show dataset-dependent accuracy for methods resolving human genomic variation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications benchmark variant, haplotype, and repeat methods against ground truth, exposing dataset-specific performance limits.

ranked.headline: Modular, reproducible software pipelines and interactive tools for omics analysis
ranked.summary: Omics analysis increasingly needs explicit, reproducible workflows, and recent tools pair that structure with LLM-assisted or interactive interfaces.

ranked.headline: Objective-driven steering of generative models for RNA and peptide design
ranked.summary: Pretrained biomolecular generators are being conditioned on RL rewards, MD ensembles, and structural restraints to target specified design objectives.

ranked.headline: Stochastic models infer selection and mutation history from single-cell and genomic data
ranked.summary: Single-cell and population genomic datasets now support explicit modeling of somatic mutation accumulation, clonal fitness, and selection from sparse or…

ranked.headline: Interaction structure and external forcing govern multispecies dynamical states
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs spatial, stochastic and network-based models with stability and amplification measures for multispecies systems.

ranked.headline: Learned and geometric methods address noise and sparsity across omics data types
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a benchmark apply ML and geometric methods to sequencing data denoising, deconvolution, and marker discovery.

ranked.headline: Cross-species single-cell and epigenomic profiling maps conserved regulatory programs
ranked.summary: Multi-omic and cross-species single-cell datasets now allow regulatory inference across brain, blood, and disease contexts.

ranked.headline: Deep learning and label-free imaging quantify cell state and tissue phenotypes
ranked.summary: Learned models now convert label-free and fluorescence microscopy into per-cell and per-organoid measurements that can be compared across conditions.

ranked.headline: Bounded geometric domains locate multi-omic signatures and tumor architecture states
ranked.summary: Explicit geometric domains now quantify multi-omic signatures, tumor architecture regimes, and spatial immune context in gastric cancer.

ranked.headline: Learned models advance enzyme design, function annotation and binding-site prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair protein language models and generative or structure-aware methods with enzyme and binding-site prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Reanalyzing existing data to adjudicate transcript structure and coding annotation
ranked.summary: Reprocessing existing RNA-seq, Ribo-Seq and long-read evidence now tests catalogue assignments of isoforms and open reading frames.

ranked.headline: Learned and physics-informed methods resolve protein conformational states in cryo-EM
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply attention-based networks and generative fiducial design to cryo-EM data to resolve protein and GPCR conformational states.

ranked.headline: Single-cell RNA-seq is now used to resolve tumor clonal structure and ecDNA selection
ranked.summary: SCANBIT and ecSingle extend scRNA-seq to tumor SNV calling and ecDNA clonal inference, alongside a harmonized copy number resource.

ranked.headline: Deep and graph learning models screen glues, GPCR ligands, antibodies and neurotoxins
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a January 2026 publication apply graph and sequence-aware deep learning to compound and biomolecule discovery.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models are individualizing brain maps from fMRI, MRI, and PET
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend individualized brain mapping with fMRI foundation models, interpretable deep networks, and faster MRI preprocessing.

ranked.headline: Kinetic, editing, and spatial structure enter transcriptomic models directly
ranked.summary: Transcriptome models are beginning to encode turnover kinetics, RNA editing, inflammatory programs, and 3D tissue geometry rather than flat counts.

ranked.headline: Image morphology and graph learning are used to infer molecular and spatial states
ranked.summary: Recent contrastive, graph, and segmentation models link tissue morphology and raw sequencing signals to spatial and molecular readouts.

ranked.headline: Assembly-scale genomes link sex chromosome evolution, mobile elements and gene loss
ranked.summary: Chromosome-level and organelle-resolved assemblies now allow mechanistic tests of mobile elements and gene loss in genome evolution.

ranked.headline: Annotation tools for repeats, isoforms, and polyadenylation sites are being benchmarked
ranked.summary: Benchmarks and pangenome analyses show that annotation method choice can shape reported gene, isoform, and repeat differences.

ranked.headline: New tools target metagenomic profiling, viral redundancy, and compositional bias
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications report large runtime and memory gains alongside benchmarks of alignment, profiling, and amplification effects.

ranked.headline: Computational methods compare protein structures beyond sequence-level similarity
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers add atom-level, binding-site, and multi-protein structural comparison methods operating at scale.

ranked.headline: Explainable models rank methylation biomarkers; transcriptomes predict protein abundance
ranked.summary: Explainable models now rank DNA methylation sites and genes as biomarkers, and predict protein abundance from transcriptomes.

ranked.headline: Genome drafts and orthogroup resources probe gene conservation and adaptation
ranked.summary: Expanding draft genomes and comparative platforms now allow direct tests of gene-family evolution across fungi, bacteria, arthropods, and protists.

ranked.headline: Curated knowledge bases unify biomarker, IBD, toxicity and drug-response data for…
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published atlas extend FAIR-oriented, curated resources linking clinical, preclinical and transcriptomic data.

ranked.headline: Metagenomic and metabolic models resolve microbiome functions in disease and environment
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs metagenome-scale analysis with metabolic modeling and homology-plus-ML screening tools across host, cattle gut, and groundwater datasets.

ranked.headline: MD simulations link allosteric dynamics to ligand and antagonist binding modes
ranked.summary: Weighted ensemble and enhanced MD with ML-derived collective variables now resolve binding and allosteric transitions in drug-relevant systems.

ranked.headline: Deep models for single-cell perturbation, annotation, and foundation-model interpretation
ranked.summary: Learned models now address single-cell perturbation prediction, annotation under batch and distribution shift, and mechanistic dissection of foundation models.

ranked.headline: Network and neural methods map multi-target drug-target interactomes
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs knowledge-graph, fragment-based neural, and curated database approaches to map drug-target interactions at interactome scale.

ranked.headline: Analytical reliability of RNA-seq through QC, normalization, and assay benchmarking
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and tools target QC, normalization, sample size, and cell calling to strengthen RNA-seq analysis reliability.

ranked.headline: Structured host and population models sharpen epidemic thresholds and strain coexistence
ranked.summary: Recent January 2026 preprints add structured transmission models with analytic thresholds, spanning behavioral, spatial, host, and phenological heterogeneity.

ranked.headline: New methods target disorder, stickiness, low-complexity regions and dynamic interfaces
ranked.summary: Preprints this month pair sequence-based disorder predictors and benchmarks with an MD-based tool for residue-level interface analysis.

ranked.headline: Software frameworks link mass spectrometry imaging with spatial and multi-omics analysis
ranked.summary: Interoperable Python tools now bring imaging mass spectrometry and general omic analysis into shared, standardized data frameworks.

ranked.headline: Hardware and algorithmic acceleration of sequence alignment and graph community detection
ranked.summary: Two preprints and one published article target throughput limits in read mapping, sequence alignment, and GPU-based graph community detection.

ranked.headline: Methods linking GWAS loci to biology via pleiotropy, epigenomes, GxE and epistasis
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 work extends GWAS interpretation to locus-process mapping, cross-ancestry gene-environment effects, and explainable epistasis inference.

ranked.headline: Models of drug-tolerant persistence, cell-size control and leukaemia trial design
ranked.summary: Agent-based and growth-curve models are being used to test resistance mechanisms and preclinical trial designs computationally.

ranked.headline: New mass spectrometry tools improve PTM quantitation and spectral library searching
ranked.summary: Recent tools expand open modification searching, single-cell histone PTM quantitation, and isotope-based metabolite identification in MS data.

ranked.headline: Simulations link proton transport and hydration to pathogenic severity
ranked.summary: Atomistic and multiscale simulations now quantify proton transport and hydration as candidate determinants of disease-linked pathogenic severity.
